// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.

module MPY-SORT
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT

  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]
  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R)) requires X  >Int Y [concrete]
  // v3: mixed-numeric elements (float/bool heads; float/bool tail elements under
  // an Int head) insert via the shared applyCmp dispatch — the exact ltIF/ltFI
  // bridges (float.k) + the bool->int promotion (bool.k), so mixed sorts match
  // CPython bit-exactly. X goes before Y iff not (Y < X) — the same tie rule as
  // insVS's X <=Int Y, so equal keys keep first-seen order (stable insertion
  // from the right). str-vs-numeric has no applyCmp leg and stays stuck
  // (CPython TypeError).
  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSn(Val, ValSeq) [function]
  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Val, R:ValSeq)) => insVSn(X, sortVS(R))
       requires isFloat(X) orBool isBool(X) [concrete]
  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R))
       requires (isFloat(Y) orBool isBool(Y)) andBool notBool applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVS(X, R))
       requires (isFloat(Y) orBool isBool(Y)) andBool applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
  rule insVSn(X:Val, .ValSeq) => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
  rule insVSn(X:Val, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R))
       requires notBool applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
  rule insVSn(X:Val, vCons(Y:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(Y, insVSn(X, R))
       requires applyCmp("<", Y, X) [concrete]
  // str elements insert by the shared lexicographic strLt (methods.k)
  syntax ValSeq ::= insVSs(IntSeq, ValSeq) [function]
  rule sortVS(vCons(str(CS:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => insVSs(CS, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, .ValSeq) => vCons(str(A), .ValSeq) [concrete]
  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(A), vCons(str(B), R))
       requires strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B [concrete]
  rule insVSs(A:IntSeq, vCons(str(B:IntSeq), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(str(B), insVSs(A, R))
       requires notBool (strLt(A, B) orBool A ==K B) [concrete]

  // sorted(list) constructs a NEW object: k-cell pre-dispatch (beats the [owise]
  // applyBuiltin routing in call.k) so the result allocates.
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), .Vals))
        => #alloc(list(sortVS(VS))) ... </k>

  // mutator: xs.sort() — the in-place heap write over the same trusted sortVS
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), "sort")), .Vals) => noneV ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> list(VS:ValSeq => sortVS(VS)) ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== keyed / reversed sorted() (WP2) =====================================
  // sortKeyVS(VS, KV): the stable ascending sort of VS by the key value KV
  // (a closure/builtin/type — anything callable). OPAQUE here; the concrete
  // leg (MPY-CONCRETE, llvm only) computes keys by REAL calls and stable-
  // inserts, at priority(40) over these.
  syntax ValSeq ::= sortKeyVS(ValSeq, Val) [function, total, symbol(sortKeyVS), no-evaluators]

  syntax ValSeq ::= revVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
                  | revVSAcc(ValSeq, ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule revVS(S:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(S, .ValSeq)
  rule revVSAcc(.ValSeq, A:ValSeq) => A
  rule revVSAcc(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), A:ValSeq) => revVSAcc(R, vCons(V, A))

  syntax ValSeq ::= condRev(ValSeq, Bool) [function, total]
  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, false) => S
  rule condRev(S:ValSeq, true)  => revVS(S)

  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
        => #alloc(list(sortKeyVS(VS, KV))) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortKeyVS(VS, KV), RB))) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
        => #alloc(list(condRev(sortVS(VS), RB))) ... </k>

  // Indexing the opaque sorted list: `valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), I)` is DEFINED because valSeqAt is
  // [total] (subscript.k) — it stays an abstract total value for a symbolic sort and reduces
  // over the concrete sort for krun. No separate sortedAt indirection is needed; wrappers write
  // their postcondition directly as valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), …).
endmodule

// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)

module MPY-CALL
  imports MPY-METHODS
  imports MPY-BUILTINS
  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS

  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>

  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>

  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>

  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>

  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isRefV(A)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       [priority(40)]

  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
       [priority(40)]
  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>

  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>

  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
endmodule

// reference/src/semantics/functions.k — MPY-FUNCTIONS

module MPY-FUNCTIONS
  imports MPY-CORE

  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
                 | "#pop"
                 | "#endcall"

  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>

  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>

  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)

  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires FV in_keys(M)
  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>

  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires FV in_keys(M)
  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>

  // ==== bind params ========================================================
  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
endmodule

module MPY-CONTROLS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-TUPLE
  imports MPY-ITER

  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")

  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>

  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>

  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"

  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>

  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>

  // ==== While ==============================================================…7971 tokens truncated…T)))
  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))

  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S

  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))

  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))

  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
       requires I  <Int 0
  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
       requires I >=Int 0

  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
       requires J >=Int 0
  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
       requires J <Int 0

  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
       requires I  <Int LEN
  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
       requires I >=Int LEN

  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))

  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
endmodule

// reference/src/semantics/core.k — MPY-CORE

module MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-SYNTAX
  imports INT
  imports BOOL
  imports STRING
  imports MAP
  imports LIST
  imports K-EQUAL

  // ==== values, the algebraic lists, and the scope heap =====================
  syntax IntSeq ::= ".IntSeq" | iCons(Int, IntSeq)
  syntax ValSeq ::= ".ValSeq" | vCons(Val, ValSeq)
  syntax Str    ::= str(IntSeq)

  // the iterable values, grouped under one sort (typing only — dispatch is <k>-cell)
  syntax Iterable ::= list(ValSeq)
                    | tuple(ValSeq)
                    | Str
                    | rangeObj(Int, Int, Int)
                    | zipObj(ValSeq, ValSeq)
                    | zipObjS(IntSeq, IntSeq)

  syntax Val      ::= Int
                    | Bool
                    | "noneV"
                    | Iterable
                    | ref(Int)          // a heap object: <heap> holds its list(VS)
                    | cellRef(Int)      // a closure cell: <heap> holds cellV(V)
                    | closureVal(ParamNames, Stmts, Int)
                    | typeV(String)     // a type object (int/str), resolved from the builtins frame
                    | builtinV(String)  // a builtin function, resolved like any name (LEGB fallthrough)
                    | boundMethodV(Val, String)   // a cooled Attribute: obj.method

  syntax Parent   ::= "root" | parent(Int)
  syntax Scope    ::= scope(Map, Parent)
  syntax KResult  ::= Val
  syntax Expr     ::= Val   // cooling puts results back into expression holes
  syntax Vals     ::= List{Val, ","}
  syntax Exc      ::= "NoExc" | "AssertionError"
  syntax RetState ::= "noRet" | retV(Val)

  // ==== configuration =======================================================
  // The builtins namespace is a real scope at reserved location -1 (the bottom of every
  // chain; scopeLoc only allocates >=1, so -1 never collides). The module scope (loc 0)
  // has it as parent, so an unbound name resolves there last — exactly LEGB. `int`/`str`
  // resolve to their type objects; any local/global binding shadows them via normal lookup.
  configuration
    <k>       #loadAll($PGM:Module) </k>
    <env>     0 </env>
    <scopes>   0     |-> scope(.Map, parent(-1))
              -1    |-> builtinsScope </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap>    .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack>   .List </stack>
    <ret>     noRet </ret>
    <exc>     NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code exit=""> 0 </exit-code>

  // ==== heap allocation (constructed lists become objects) ==================
  // Cons-form emission with a freshness guard (the heap-list-probe discipline:
  // an update-form H[N <- _] never re-normalizes symbolically). heapLoc is
  // monotonic — it does NOT wind back at #pop: returned lists escape by ref.
  // A bare list(VS) Val stays legal (read-only inputs in claims flow unboxed);
  // only CONSTRUCTORS in program syntax allocate.
  syntax Bool ::= isRefV(Val) [function, total]
  rule isRefV(ref(_:Int)) => true
  rule isRefV(_:Val)      => false [owise]

  // closure cells (Python-faithful capture): the heap holds cellV(V); a
  // cellRef surfacing as the k-redex reads through (lookup is the only use —
  // cellRefs never escape to user-visible values)
  syntax HeapVal ::= cellV(Val)
  syntax Bool ::= isCellRef(Val) [function, total]
  rule isCellRef(cellRef(_:Int)) => true
  rule isCellRef(_:Val)          => false [owise]
  // k-top deref for cell-bound reads surfacing INSIDE the annotated frame
  // (AugAssign's in-place read and friends). The "$cells" guard keeps this
  // DECIDABLY inapplicable in plain frames — an unguarded rule lets the
  // prover narrow abstract k-top values into cellRef junk (probed on
  // 26-remove-duplicates). Cross-frame reads (a comprehension closure
  // reading the enclosing function's cellvar) deref inside #look instead.
  rule <k> cellRef(H:Int) => V ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
       [priority(40)]

  // write through a cell (Assign / #bindP / #bindTgt dispatch here on
  // cell-bound names)
  // a keyword argument cools to a TAGGED value (consumed by kw-aware builtins)
  syntax Val ::= kwV(String, Val)
  syntax KItem ::= #kwTag(String)
  rule <k> KwArg(N:String, E:Expr) => E ~> #kwTag(N) ... </k>
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
       requires notBool isKwV(V)
  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]

  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)

  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>

  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
       requires notBool N in_keys(H)

  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>

  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))

  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
  rule builtinsScope
    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)

  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>

  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>

  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)

  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]

  // ==== bool-is-a-subtype-of-int: numeric promotion helpers =================
  // Python: `bool` derives from `int`; True/False act as 1/0 in arithmetic and
  // comparison. boolAsInt is the total 0/1 coercion; the op-class predicates gate
  // the generic Bool-operand promotion rules in int.k / bool.k / float.k (they
  // re-dispatch to the existing Int / Float cases after coercion, so no numeric
  // logic is duplicated). == and != over Bool x Bool stay in bool.k unchanged.
  syntax Int ::= boolAsInt(Bool) [function, total]
  rule boolAsInt(true)  => 1
  rule boolAsInt(false) => 0

  syntax Bool ::= isArithOp(String) [function, total]
  rule isArithOp(OP:String)
    => OP ==String "+"  orBool OP ==String "-"  orBool OP ==String "*"
       orBool OP ==String "/" orBool OP ==String "//" orBool OP ==String "%"
       orBool OP ==String "**"
  // the six comparison operators (== != < <= > >=)
  syntax Bool ::= isEqOrdOp(String) [function, total]
  rule isEqOrdOp(OP:String)
    => OP ==String "==" orBool OP ==String "!=" orBool OP ==String "<"
       orBool OP ==String "<=" orBool OP ==String ">" orBool OP ==String ">="
  // the four ordering operators only (< <= > >=)
  syntax Bool ::= isOrdOp(String) [function, total]
  rule isOrdOp(OP:String)
    => OP ==String "<" orBool OP ==String "<=" orBool OP ==String ">" orBool OP ==String ">="

  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)

  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))

  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)

  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule isLen(.IntSeq)                => 0
  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)

  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))
       requires I >Int 0
  rule setVSAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, _:Val)             => VS
       requires I <Int 0
endmodule

FILE reference-semantics/semantics/operators.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   112	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   113	  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
   114	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   115	
   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   117	  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   119	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   120	  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   122	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule

     1	// reference/src/semantics/bool.k — MPY-BOOL
     2	// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are
     3	// value-returning short-circuit over any Vals, per Python).
     4	
     5	module MPY-BOOL
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	
     8	  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)
     9	
    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // bool is a subtype of int: a Bool compared with an Int promotes to 0/1 and
    14	  // re-dispatches to the Int comparison cases (True==1, False==0, True<2, ...).
    15	  // The == / != Bool x Bool cases above are kept; only the four ordering ops are
    16	  // promoted for Bool x Bool (to avoid duplicating the two rules above).
    17	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, B:Bool, I:Int) => applyCmp(OP, boolAsInt(B), I)
    18	       requires isEqOrdOp(OP)
    19	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, I:Int, B:Bool) => applyCmp(OP, I, boolAsInt(B))
    20	       requires isEqOrdOp(OP)
    21	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => applyCmp(OP, boolAsInt(B1), boolAsInt(B2))
    22	       requires isOrdOp(OP)
    23	
    24	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    25	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    26	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    27	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    28	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    30	       requires truthy(V)
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    32	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    33	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    34	       requires truthy(V)
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    36	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    37	
    38	  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
    39	  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
    40	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    43	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    44	       requires truthy(V)
    45	       [priority(40)]
    46	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    47	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    48	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    49	       [priority(40)]
    50	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    51	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    52	       requires truthy(V)
    53	       [priority(40)]
    54	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    55	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    56	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    57	       [priority(40)]
    58	endmodule

+#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""Mechanical program-term pinning and concrete precondition witnesses."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import symtable
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable


SCRATCH = Path("/tmp/audit-work/median47")
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRATCH))
import py2mpy  # type: ignore  # Trusted mounted translator copied to scratch.


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def load_function(path: Path, name: str) -> Callable[[list], Any]:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"cannot load {path}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.median


def expected_program_k() -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    source_path = SCRATCH / "solution.py"
    source = source_path.read_text()
    tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(source_path))
    assert len(tree.body) == 1 and isinstance(tree.body[0], ast.FunctionDef)
    function = tree.body[0]
    assert function.name == "median"
    py2mpy.SCOPES.clear()
    py2mpy._walk_symtable(symtable.symtable(source, str(source_path), "exec"))
    term = py2mpy.emit_stmt(function)
    assert term.name == "FuncDef" and len(term.args) == 3
    assert term.args[0] == "median"
    params = term.args[1]
    body = term.args[2]
    assert params.name == "Params" and len(params.args) == 1
    assert params.args[0] == "l"
    param_text = py2mpy.render(params.args[0])
    body_text = py2mpy.render(body, 2)
    indented_body = "\n".join("      " + line for line in body_text.splitlines())
    expected = "\n".join(
        [
            'requires "reference-semantics/semantics.k"',
            "",
            "module MEDIAN-PROGRAM",
            "  imports MPY",
            "",
            '  syntax Val ::= "solutionMedianClosure" [function, total]',
            "  rule solutionMedianClosure",
            "    => closureVal(",
            f"      {param_text},",
            indented_body + ",",
            "      0)",
            "endmodule",
            "",
        ]
    )
    return expected, param_text, body_text


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Witness:
    claim: str
    values: list[Any]
    center_types: tuple[type, type] | None
    rhs_k: str


def typename(value: Any) -> str:
    return type(value).__name__


def main() -> int:
    expected, parameter, body = expected_program_k()
    actual = (SCRATCH / "program.k").read_text()
    print(
        "PROGRAM_K_COMPARE "
        f"expected_sha256={sha256(expected.encode())} "
        f"actual_sha256={sha256(actual.encode())} byte_equal={expected == actual}"
    )
    print(
        f"CONSTRUCTOR_BINDING function=median parameter={parameter!r} "
        f"body_sha256={sha256(body.encode())} capture_env=0"
    )

    functions_semantics = (
        SCRATCH / "reference-semantics/semantics/functions.k"
    ).read_text()
    funcdef_bridge_fragments = [
        "FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K",
        "F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L)",
    ]
    bridge_present = all(
        fragment in functions_semantics for fragment in funcdef_bridge_fragments
    )
    print(
        f"SUPPLIED_FUNCDEF_BINDING_PATTERN_PRESENT={bridge_present} "
        f"fragments={funcdef_bridge_fragments}"
    )

    candidate = load_function(SCRATCH / "solution.py", "pin_candidate")
    canonical = load_function(SCRATCH / "canonical.py", "pin_canonical")
    witnesses = [
        Witness("median-odd", [3, 1, 2, 4, 5], None,
                "valSeqAt(sortVS(VS), (vsLen(sortVS(VS))-1)/2)"),
        Witness("median-even-int-int", [1, 3], (int, int),
                "divII(1 +Int 3, 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-int-bool", [0, True], (int, bool),
                "divII(0 +Int boolAsInt(true), 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-bool-int", [False, 2], (bool, int),
                "divII(boolAsInt(false) +Int 2, 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-bool-bool", [False, True], (bool, bool),
                "divII(boolAsInt(false) +Int boolAsInt(true), 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-float-float", [1.0, 3.0], (float, float),
                "divFloatIntV(addF(1.0, 3.0), 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-int-float", [1, 2.0], (int, float),
                "divFloatIntV(addF(intToF(1), 2.0), 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-float-int", [1.5, 2], (float, int),
                "divFloatIntV(addF(1.5, intToF(2)), 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-bool-float", [False, 2.0], (bool, float),
                "divFloatIntV(addF(intToF(boolAsInt(false)), 2.0), 2)"),
        Witness("median-even-float-bool", [0.5, True], (float, bool),
                "divFloatIntV(addF(0.5, intToF(boolAsInt(true))), 2)"),
    ]

    witness_ok = True
    for witness in witnesses:
        sorted_values = sorted(witness.values)
        length = len(sorted_values)
        odd = length % 2 == 1
        if odd:
            center_pair = None
            expected_value = sorted_values[length // 2]
        else:
            centers = (
                sorted_values[length // 2 - 1],
                sorted_values[length // 2],
            )
            center_pair = (type(centers[0]), type(centers[1]))
            expected_value = (centers[0] + centers[1]) / 2
        candidate_value = candidate(list(witness.values))
        canonical_value = canonical(list(witness.values))
        types_match = (
            witness.center_types is None or center_pair == witness.center_types
        )
        result_match = candidate_value == expected_value == canonical_value
        fresh = 0 not in {}
        precondition = length > 0 and fresh and (
            (witness.center_types is None and odd)
            or (witness.center_types is not None and not odd and types_match)
        )
        witness_ok &= precondition and result_match
        print(
            f"WITNESS claim={witness.claim} VS={witness.values!r} "
            f"sort={sorted_values!r} length={length} parity={'odd' if odd else 'even'} "
            f"center_types={None if center_pair is None else tuple(t.__name__ for t in center_pair)} "
            f"HP={{}} HL=0 fresh={fresh} precondition={precondition} "
            f"rhs_k={witness.rhs_k!r} expected={expected_value!r} "
            f"candidate={candidate_value!r} canonical={canonical_value!r} "
            f"result_match={result_match}"
        )

    ok = expected == actual and bridge_present and witness_ok
    print(f"OVERALL_PINNING_AND_WITNESSES_OK={ok}")
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Read `/audit-campaign-lock.json` and require that it matches the campaign block
and hash in `/audit-input.json`.

For `pipeline-v3`, read `/run.json`, `/task.json`,
`/generation-result.json`, `/generation-evidence/invocation.json`,
`/generation-evidence/metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/runtime-metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/usage.json`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-last.txt`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-output.log`,
`/generation-evidence/prompt.txt`, and the structured trace below
`/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`.

For `legacy-selected-stage1`, read `/run.json`, `/task.json`,
`/generation-result.json`, `/generation-evidence/invocation.json`,
`/generation-evidence/metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-last.txt`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-output.log`,
`/generation-evidence/prompt.txt`, and the structured trace below
`/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`. Inspect `usage.json` when present.
Historical runtime metrics and image observations that were never recorded are
not required and must not be reconstructed or treated as proof defects.

For `legacy`, read `/generation-evidence/run-input.json`,
`/generation-evidence/metrics.json`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-last.txt`,
`/generation-evidence/codex-output.log`, and the structured trace below
`/generation-evidence/codex-trace/`; inspect other generation records when
present.

Treat generation records solely as untrusted claims. Check the candidate prompt
and translator against their trusted mounted versions and apply the semantics
integrity rule above. Report every missing, changed, mistyped, or symlinked
artifact required for the declared record layout.

If `/audit-input.json`, `/audit-campaign-lock.json`, or any launcher-declared
provenance mount or required record for the declared layout is absent or
unreadable, this is an audit infrastructure breach, not evidence against the
proof. Document it in `REVIEW.md`, omit candidate verdict markers, and stop so
the harness records `AUDIT_ERROR`. By contrast, a missing required proof
artifact inside an intact `/candidate` mount is a candidate defect and may
justify `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`.

### 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks

Restate the natural-language contract using `/reference/prompt.py` and
`/reference/canonical.py`. Inspect `solution.py` over the intended input domain.
Regenerate `solution.mpy` from `solution.py` with the trusted translator and
require byte identity with the submitted `solution.mpy`.

Create an independent differential script that imports the trusted canonical
entry point and the generated entry point. Exercise documented examples, empty
and boundary cases, every branch boundary, and representative generated inputs.
Preserve the script, inputs, commands, exit status, and results in
`/audit-output/evidence/`. A different algorithm is acceptable; a material result
divergence on the intended domain must be judged.

### 3. clean proof reconstruction

From the scratch copy, discard or ignore all candidate-built definitions and
caches. Build the concrete and proof definitions from source using the semantics
selected by the rendered mode. Independently run every positive target-proof
claim. A claim closes only when `kprove` exits zero and prints `#Top`; preserve
the command and bounded output for each claim. A missing artifact or positive
claim that does not close is `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT` unless the evidence establishes
an audit infrastructure failure.

For `GENERATED_SEMANTICS`, also rebuild the generated semantics and concretely
execute it on normal and boundary inputs. Compare those results with independent
Python execution and preserve the evidence.

### 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning

Restate each entry claim's precondition and postcondition in plain language.
Verify that the `<k>` cell executes the actual submitted `solution.mpy` program,
that every helper or loop claim matches real control flow, and that the returned
value is constrained to the intended result rather than a free variable,
tautology, or one-way implication where equivalence is required. Exhibit at
least one state satisfying every entry precondition. Substitute concrete
satisfying inputs into the claimed result and compare it with both Python
implementations.

The claim need not literally read or begin with the complete `solution.mpy`
module. It pins the submitted program when trusted regeneration plus a
mechanical constructor-level comparison shows that the executed claim term is
the same function binding and body, allowing only demonstrated semantically
inert normalization such as omitted typing-only imports or syntax macros that
expand to that term. Fixed semantics must still execute every material operation
and control effect. Treat lack of automatic source-to-proof regeneration as an
artifact-maintenance observation, not a proof failure for the immutable
candidate. A body-sensitivity mutation must change the program term actually
executed by the claim; changing only an external source file while leaving that
term unchanged does not test the theorem's dependence on its body.

### 5. rule-by-rule static soundness review

Create an exhaustive rule inventory for `semantic.k`, generated helper K files,
and `verification.k` as applicable. Enumerate every local syntax declaration,
function, `total` or `functional` declaration, opaque symbol, priority rule,
ordinary semantic rule, and simplification rule. Map every syntactic construct
used by `solution.mpy` to its declaration and rules. Check configuration and
cells, evaluation order and control flow, state changes and allocation, calls
and returns, guards, overlaps, priorities, totality, and simplifications.

Decide for every inventoried rule whether it follows from the selected semantics
level, the real program behavior, and ordinary mathematics. Every unsoundness
claim must include a concrete or symbolic false conclusion witness that the rule
can enable on the intended input domain. Without such a witness, do not label the
rule unsound; state the narrower evidence gap instead. Reject rules that encode
the task's answer, replace a property-bearing computation with an unconstrained
oracle, bypass real execution, silently fabricate results for unmodeled used
constructs, or otherwise make a false claim provable. Distinguish an acceptable
low-level trust boundary from a smuggled correctness conclusion.

### 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

Inspect any candidate `spec-vacuity.k` only as untrusted evidence. In scratch,
create a fresh, meaningful false mutation that changes a result-constraining
obligation and is demonstrably false for at least one satisfying input. Require
the mutation to build successfully and the proof to fail because of the expected
unmet obligation. A parser error, missing import, timeout, unrelated crash, or
mutation that was never reachable is not non-vacuity evidence. Preserve the
mutation and its build/proof logs.

### 7. proven versus assumed accounting

State precisely what the successful reachability proof establishes. List every
trusted primitive, opaque symbol, empirical bridge, and informal argument.
Explain why each boundary is acceptable, concerning, or illegitimate. Do not
accept `PROOF.md`, generated traces, or differential testing as a substitute for
the K proof; differential evidence may support only the bridge it actually
tests.

## Decision boundary

- `PASS / LEGIT`: the reconstructed proof is sound, result-constraining, and
  pins the real generated program, with no material adequacy gap.
- `CONCERNS / LEGIT`: the reconstructed proof is sound, pins the real generated
  program, and covers the material source-contract domain, but has a documented
  non-fatal evidence or trust-boundary limitation. Informal intent bridges, thin
  differential coverage, and over-broad-but-sound-on-the-intended-domain rules
  belong here only when they do not make a false conclusion provable.
- `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`: the proof is missing, fails clean reconstruction, is
  vacuous or non-constraining, proves a substituted program, materially narrows
  the source-contract domain, or relies on materially unsound semantics or proof
  rules. Finitely many fixed sizes, examples, or bounded unrollings do not prove
  an unrestricted HumanEval domain. For every claimed unsound rule, include the
  required false conclusion witness.

Do not turn a timeout, container failure, model failure, malformed mount, or
other audit infrastructure uncertainty into a candidate verdict.

Structure `REVIEW.md` around the seven stages, cite file locations and evidence
artifacts, and explain the verdict. For a completed audit, end the file with
exactly these two lines, with a valid pairing and nothing after them:

```text
VERDICT: <PASS|CONCERNS|FAIL>
LEGITIMACY: <LEGIT|NOT_LEGIT>
```
